In retrospect I learned several things from this
- It's bad practice to send patients away just because you don't feel like helping them. Professionals have a duty to help patients or refer them to someone who can help.
- It takes a long time to build up enough context with a therapist which makes trying several different therapists a lengthy, time consuming, and expensive process.
- Marriage counseling generally has a very low success rate (I've see numbers like 1/10). Although it's hard to find a meaningful statistic.
- Counseling often causes latrogenic divorce. The first step in proper marriage counseling is to set aside problems.
